column2: Under the Stars

The pyre for [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] burned until dawn, and still I cannot believe it. The plague took [grief_dead_one.GetHerHim] in days. One morning [grief_dead_one.GetSheHe] was laughing at my table, and a week later the corpse-carts came.\n\nTonight I climbed the tower and looked up at the stars, the way we used to when we were young. Morrslieb hangs low and green over the hills. Somewhere beyond it, they say, Morr keeps his gardens of the dead. I hope [grief_dead_one.GetSheHe] walks there in peace.
How can [grief_dead_one.GetSheHe] be gone?

The days pass, and the court goes about its business as if nothing has happened. The servants whisper when I pass. My councillors bring me petitions and grain counts. Nobody speaks [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName]'s name, as if the plague might hear it and come back.

I have stood by a hundred deathbeds and spoken the rites of passing over the dead. I have told widows and orphans that the gods hold their loved ones now. The words come easily when the dead are strangers. Now [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] is gone, and the words are ashes in my mouth.
I should speak to someone about this.
I only wish [grief_dead_one.GetSheHe] were here.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been watching me for days, I am sure of it. Today [From.GetSheHe] finally came to me in the gallery.\n\n"Forgive me. I have seen how you look since [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] died, and I have wanted to speak to you, but I did not know how. I miss [grief_dead_one.GetHerHim] too. I thought... perhaps we could miss [grief_dead_one.GetHerHim] together."
Thank you. I am not as strong as everyone thinks.
I am FINE. I said I am FINE!

[grief_friend.GetFirstName] has come to see me again, and this time [grief_friend.GetSheHe] brought something: a small grey owl, sleepy-eyed and ruffled, perched on [grief_friend.GetHerHis] glove. It was [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName]'s owl. Nobody could bear to look after it.\n\n"Verena's bird," [grief_friend.GetSheHe] says. "Wise, and patient. I think [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] would want you to have her."
Oh, look at her! I will take good care of her.
I can barely take care of myself.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] stays behind after the council meeting, fiddling with [From.GetHerHis] papers until the others are gone.\n\n"Forgive me, but the whole court has noticed. You and [grief_friend.GetFirstName] are always together these days. It is good to see you smile again. Is it true that you have become friends?"
Our grief has brought us together.
I have no idea what you are talking about.

[From.GetFirstName] comes to my chambers late in the evening, pale and fidgeting. [From.GetSheHeCap] barely greets me before [From.GetSheHe] asks: "The owl... could I have her back? Only for a while. I cannot sleep, and I keep thinking of [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName]."\n\n[From.GetHerHisCap] hands are shaking. Something is wrong.

[From.GetFirstName] comes to my chambers late in the evening, pale and fidgeting. [From.GetSheHeCap] sits down without a word, stands again, goes to the window and stares out into the dark.\n\n[From.GetHerHisCap] hands are shaking. Something is wrong.
Sit down. Tell me what is wrong.
Leave me be! I have enough troubles of my own!
It does not concern me.

At last [grief_friend.GetFirstName] whispers it. The fever came three days ago. The sweats at night. A swelling under [grief_friend.GetHerHis] arm that [grief_friend.GetSheHe] has shown no one.\n\n"It is the same," [grief_friend.GetSheHe] says. "The same as [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName]. I am going to die like [grief_dead_one.GetSheHe] did."
It may not be the plague. Not every fever kills.

[grief_friend.GetFirstName] opens [grief_friend.GetHerHis] mouth, closes it again, and then begins to weep. [grief_friend.GetSheHeCap] cries until [grief_friend.GetHerHis] shoulders shake and will not say why. After a long time [grief_friend.GetSheHe] wipes [grief_friend.GetHerHis] face and leaves without a word.
[grief_friend.GetSheHeCap] will talk when [grief_friend.GetSheHe] is ready.

[grief_friend.GetFirstName] stares at me as if I had struck [grief_friend.GetHerHim].\n\n"I thought you of all people would understand. But you never cared for [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName], did you? And you do not care for me. Curse you, and curse your cold heart!"
Leave, then.
[grief_friend.GetFirstName] will not come back to you.

[From.GetFirstName] asks me to ride out with [From.GetHerHim] to the hills where [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] used to hunt. For a whole day we follow the owl over the heather and talk about everything and nothing. [From.GetSheHeCap] coughs now and then and waves it away.

The fever has not let go of [From.GetFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] lies in a darkened room with the shutters closed, and the physicians come and go with their bowls and leeches. When I come in, [From.GetSheHe] smiles and reaches for my hand.
I will sit with [From.GetHerHim] as long as it takes.
You stay by [From.GetFirstName]'s side through the fever.
Let us ride out again tomorrow.
You spend the next weeks together.
The Fever Breaks

On the ninth night the fever broke. [grief_friend.GetFirstName] woke soaked in sweat and asked for bread, and the physicians swore it was a miracle. It was not the plague after all, or the plague was not hungry for another of us.\n\nThis morning we walked in the garden together, slowly, [grief_friend.GetHerHim] leaning on my arm.

Whatever troubled [grief_friend.GetFirstName] has passed. [grief_friend.GetSheHeCap] laughs again, and eats again, and this morning we walked in the garden together and spoke of [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] without weeping.
I knew it was nothing to worry about.
Thank the gods.
[grief_friend.GetFirstName] lives.
The Plague Comes Again

The physicians could do nothing. [grief_friend.GetFirstName] died before dawn, with the swellings black under [grief_friend.GetHerHis] arms and my hand in [grief_friend.GetHerHis]. [grief_friend.GetSheHeCap] was the same age [grief_dead_one.GetFirstName] was.\n\nThe corpse-carts came again. I watched them from the tower until they were gone.

They found [grief_friend.GetFirstName] in [grief_friend.GetHerHis] bed this morning, already cold. The plague had been in [grief_friend.GetHerHim] for weeks, and [grief_friend.GetSheHe] told no one. Not even me.\n\nThe corpse-carts came again. I watched them from the tower until they were gone.
Life is so cruel.
[grief_friend.GetFirstName] is dead.
The Wedding Feast

The hall is loud with music and toasts. My new spouse sits beside me, the guests drink to our health, and the minstrels sing the old songs of love and valour. I should be the happiest [Root.GetManWoman] in the world.\n\nAnd yet my eyes keep wandering across the hall, to [From.GetTitledName], who sits beside [From.GetHerHis] own spouse. [From.GetSheHeCap] laughs at something, catches my eye, and looks away.
Who is that?

Later, when the tables have been pushed back for the dancing, I find myself standing beside [From.GetFirstName]. We talk about nothing: the music, the wine, the weather. [From.GetSheHeCap] is witty and warm, and when the musicians strike up the next dance, [From.GetSheHe] takes my hand as if it were the most natural thing in the world.\n\nMy spouse is watching from the high table.
Dance with [From.GetHerHim].
My place is with my new spouse.

I dreamt of [From.GetFirstName] last night. We walked together by a lake, and the mist lay on the water, and [From.GetSheHe] told me things I could never repeat in daylight.\n\nThe guests are leaving the castle in the morning. If I want to see [From.GetHerHim] again, it must be today.
I must find [From.GetHerHim] before [From.GetSheHe] leaves.
This is wrong. I am married.

I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the garden, among the roses. When I told [From.GetHerHim] what I felt, [From.GetSheHe] listened, and smiled sadly, and shook [From.GetHerHis] head.\n\n"You are kind, and I am flattered. But you have a spouse, and so do I, and we both swore before the gods. Let us part as friends."
As you wish...

Months have passed, and I still cannot forget [courtly_lover.GetFirstName]. The minstrels say the knights of old won their ladies with deeds and verses, and a love that waits and serves is the noblest of all. Perhaps a few words of verse would tell [courtly_lover.GetHerHim] what I cannot say aloud.
I will write [courtly_lover.GetHerHim] a poem.
The poem may turn out well...
...or it may not.
I will write [courtly_lover.GetHerHim] the finest poem I have ever written.
Words are cheap. I will send a gift instead.
Better to send nothing at all.

I wrote all night, by the light of a single candle, and when the sun rose the poem was finished. It is good. It may be the best thing I have ever written. Every line sings of [courtly_lover.GetFirstName].
Seal it and send it.

I wrote all night, by the light of a single candle, and when the sun rose I read the poem through. It is dreadful. The rhymes limp, the metaphors drown, and the line comparing [courtly_lover.GetFirstName]'s eyes to two stewed plums is beyond saving.
Send it anyway. It is the thought that counts.
Burn it and send a gift instead.

My dear friend,

I have read your poem a dozen times, and I keep it under my pillow where nobody will find it. I did not know anyone could see me the way you see me. I should not write this, but I cannot stop thinking of you.

[From.GetFirstName]

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I have received your poem. I do not know what to say about it, so I shall say nothing, and I beg you not to write to me again.

[From.GetFirstName]

My dear friend,

Your gift arrived today. It is beautiful, and I have no right to keep it, and I am keeping it all the same. I wear it when my spouse is away.

[From.GetFirstName]
[From.GetSheHeCap] loved it!
[From.GetSheHeCap] hated it...
[From.GetSheHeCap] loved the gift!

Letters have gone back and forth for months now, carried by the most discreet of my servants. Now a new letter has come, sealed with [courtly_lover.GetFirstName]'s seal. [courtly_rival.GetTitledFirstName] is holding a great hunt at [courtly_rival.GetHerHis] lodge in the forest, and [courtly_lover.GetFirstName] writes that I would be most welcome.
I will go.
It is too dangerous. I will stay home.

The lodge is full of hunters, hounds and noise. At dinner I am seated far down the table from [From.GetFirstName], who sits beside [courtly_rival.GetFirstName] at the head. Now and then our eyes meet across the candles and the roast boar.
I must find a way to speak to [From.GetHerHim].
I will keep my distance and watch.

I tried to catch [courtly_lover.GetFirstName] alone after dinner, but [From.GetFirstName] was always there, at [courtly_lover.GetHerHis] elbow. When I finally gave up, I turned to find [From.GetFirstName] watching me with narrowed eyes.
Did [From.GetSheHe] notice?

On the last day of the hunt the party scatters through the forest after a great boar. I have lost the others among the trees when a scream rings out ahead, a scream I would know anywhere. It is [courtly_lover.GetFirstName].
Run towards it!
It is none of my business.

I burst into the clearing. [From.GetFirstName] has been thrown from [From.GetHerHis] horse and lies against a fallen oak. Before [From.GetHerHim] stands the boar: a scarred old monster as big as a pony, with tusks like daggers and blood on its snout. It paws the ground, ready to charge.
Shoot it!
You may kill the boar before it charges.
Charge the beast with my spear!
You will probably kill the boar.
I cannot move...
[From.GetFirstName] may die.

The hunters found [courtly_lover.GetFirstName] at dusk, at the foot of a fallen oak, gored by the boar. They say [courtly_lover.GetSheHe] lived for a while after the beast was gone, and called out for help, and nobody came.
I should have gone to [courtly_lover.GetHerHim].

My arrow took the boar behind the shoulder, and it crashed to the ground a spear's length from [From.GetFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] threw [From.GetHerHis] arms around me, trembling, and before either of us knew it, [From.GetSheHe] kissed me.

My arrow went wide. The boar charged, and [From.GetFirstName]'s scream was cut short. By the time the other hunters came, the beast was gone into the trees, and [From.GetFirstName] lay broken in the leaves.
I ran at the beast with my spear and drove it home. The boar thrashed and died at my feet. [From.GetFirstName] stumbled to me, trembling, and before either of us knew it, [From.GetSheHe] kissed me.

I ran at the beast with my spear and drove it home, but its tusk caught me as it fell. Bleeding, I knelt by [From.GetFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] pressed [From.GetHerHis] cloak to my wound with shaking hands, and kissed me.
I stood frozen at the edge of the clearing while the boar charged. By the time my legs would move again, the beast had gone back into the trees, and [From.GetFirstName] lay in the leaves.
I love you.
We cannot. Not like this.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is crippled... and it is my fault.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is dead.

The days after the hunt pass like a dream. [courtly_lover.GetFirstName] and I meet in the corners of the lodge, in the stables, in the woods. [courtly_rival.GetFirstName] suspects nothing yet, or seems not to.\n\nBut the hunt will end soon, and we will go back to our own halls.
One more secret meeting, tonight.
We will wait for the next hunt.
The hunt is over and the guests ride home. The boar's head hangs over [courtly_rival.GetFirstName]'s hearth, and the tale of the hunt is already growing in the telling.
What a hunt it was.

The door burst open and there stood [From.GetFirstName], with a candle in [From.GetHerHis] hand and murder in [From.GetHerHis] eyes. By morning the whole lodge knew. By the end of the month the whole realm will know.
[From.GetSheHeCap] will never forgive me.

My love,

I cannot bear it any longer. Every day with [courtly_rival.GetFirstName] is a prison. [courtly_rival.GetSheHeCap] watches me, [courtly_rival.GetSheHe] reads my letters, [courtly_rival.GetSheHe] will never let me go. If you love me, find a way to free me. Any way.

[From.GetFirstName]
I will free you.
I cannot do this. It is over.

[courtly_rival.GetTitledFirstName] stands between me and [courtly_lover.GetFirstName]. Something must be done about [courtly_rival.GetHerHim]. I could challenge [courtly_rival.GetHerHim] openly and settle it with steel, or try to reason with [courtly_rival.GetHerHim], or... there are quieter ways.
A duel to the death!
I will talk some sense into [courtly_rival.GetHerHim].
A knife in the dark.
You have shamed me and my house. Meet me at dawn on the first day of next month, with sword and shield, and let the gods judge between us.\n\n[From.GetTitledName]
I will be there.

We met at dawn on the field below [courtly_rival.GetFirstName]'s castle. [courtly_rival.GetSheHeCap] fought well, and long, but in the end [courtly_rival.GetSheHe] slipped on the wet grass and my blade found [courtly_rival.GetHerHis] heart.
It is done.
We met at dawn on the field below [courtly_rival.GetFirstName]'s castle. [courtly_rival.GetSheHeCap] was stronger than I thought, and faster. My shield split, my sword arm went numb, and I fell.
No...
You may die of your wounds.

I spoke with [courtly_rival.GetFirstName] for a long time, face to face and heart to heart. [courtly_rival.GetSheHeCap] raged, then wept, and in the end [courtly_rival.GetSheHe] admitted that [courtly_rival.GetHerHis] marriage was a cold and empty thing. [courtly_rival.GetSheHeCap] will set [courtly_lover.GetFirstName] free.
It is for the best.

I tried to reason with [courtly_rival.GetFirstName], but [courtly_rival.GetSheHe] would not hear a word of it. [courtly_rival.GetSheHeCap] threw me out of [courtly_rival.GetHerHis] hall and swore that I would never see [courtly_lover.GetFirstName] again.
Then it is over.

[courtly_rival.GetFirstName] went hunting alone, as [courtly_rival.GetSheHe] often does. An arrow from the trees found [courtly_rival.GetHerHis] throat. Nobody saw the archer, and the archer has already left the realm with a fat purse.
A tragic accident.
My hired blade was caught in [courtly_rival.GetFirstName]'s woods with a bow in his hands and my gold in his purse. Under the hot irons he told them everything. Now everyone knows what I tried to do.
Curse the fool!
Together at Last
[From.GetFirstName] is free, and [From.GetSheHe] has come to me. Let the court whisper. We walk together in the garden in the evenings, and the minstrels have already begun a song about us.
Nothing can part us now.
What Might Have Been

Sometimes, in the evenings, I walk alone in the garden and think of [courtly_lover.GetFirstName], and of everything that might have been. Then the bells ring for supper, and I go back inside to my spouse, and my duties, and my life.
It was never meant to be.
